preamble: In the uvular-r area of northwestern Europe, the voiced uvular fricative or approximant [ʁ] is vocalized in the syllable coda to the near-open central vowel [ɐ], filed here under the nearest open vowel. Standard German has [ʁ] in onsets but [ɐ] for word-final -er and a non-syllabic [ɐ̯] after stressed vowels (Oper [ˈoːpɐ], wir [viːɐ̯]); Standard Danish has [ʁ] syllable-initially and [ɐ̯] syllable-finally; and younger speakers of Luxembourgish vocalize coda /r/ to [ɐ] in the same way, while older speakers keep a consonantal [ʀ ~ ʁ].

examples.note: Word-final unstressed /ər/ is realized as syllabic [ɐ].
After stressed vowels coda /r/ becomes non-syllabic [ɐ̯], forming centering diphthongs, as in mehr [meːɐ̯] 'more' and Tor [toːɐ̯] 'gate'.

examples.from: stærkeste, coda /r/ (syllable-initial /r/ is [ʁ], as in brød [ˈpʁœ̝ðˀ])

examples.note: Younger speakers vocalize word-final /r/ to [ɐ], as in German and Danish.

examples.from: wier, coda /r/ after a long vowel
